title: Excessive Object Pooling of Lightweight Non-I/O Objects
pattern: Implementing or instantiating thread-safe object pools (e.g., lock-guarded pools) for lightweight, short-lived memory structures that do not represent external system sockets, threads, or descriptors.
why_bad: Object pooling introduces significant bookkeeping, synchronization, and atomic instruction overhead [237]. For ordinary, cheap memory-only objects, the CPU overhead required to synchronize pool checkouts is dramatically worse than simply constructing/allocating the object on the stack or heap [237]. Object pooling should be strictly reserved for heavy I/O connections or OS threads [237].
detection: Identify instantiations of object pools where the pooled type does not encapsulate an I/O resource, database connection, or system process thread.
fix: Do not pool cheap, lightweight, memory-only objects; let the compiler, allocator, and stack handle standard allocation/dropping [238].
source: Michael T. Nygard, *Release It!*, Chapter 10 (Keep It Up) / passages [237, 238].
